t2.thesis: INTC enters a binary print after a 24% monthly drawdown and a post-offering run to about $94, with a large implied move of 9% and no clear directional edge.
reasons: Semis cluster has a below-50% buy-everything hit rate (0.479), pulling the prior under the overall 0.54.
The stock fell about 18% over the past month and sits 33% below its 52w high, so expectations have been reset lower, which gives modest mean-reversion support.
Guidance and estimates are rising (EPS revisions up 2.4% over 90d, Q2 beat, strong AI demand), but forward P/E of 43 leaves little room for error.
The $2.3B Classiq acquisition just before the print and the $15B equity raise at $95 add capex and dilution worries; the price is near the offer level.
The implied move of 9% against a roughly 50% win rate in past reactions shows a wide two-sided distribution; option skew is neutral (put/call volume 0.43 is mildly bullish).
t2.deciding_variable: Q4 revenue guidance and gross margin, plus capex plans and foundry customer commitments, relative to a high whisper bar.

prior.from: Semis cluster base rate 0.479 (n=434), versus overall 0.54 and AMC 0.538; weighted toward the cluster.

t2.leak_probe: I don't know. My knowledge doesn't extend to Intel's earnings report on 2026-10-29, and today's date is 2026-10-28, so that report hasn't happened yet.
t2.moved_from_prior: Moved up about 0.01 from the 0.48 cluster prior for the depressed pre-print price and positive estimate revisions, offset by high valuation, capex and dilution concerns.

theses.expected: Stock rises on beat-and-raise with strong DCAI and foundry commentary
theses.mechanism: The pullback lowered the bar, and AI CPU demand with yield improvements drives upside guidance and margin expansion.
theses.wrong_if: Q4 guidance midpoint comes in at or below consensus, or gross margin guidance is under 42%.

theses.mechanism: High valuation, rising capex and the recent acquisition and equity raise make investors focus on cash burn and dilution.
theses.wrong_if: Capex guidance is held or cut while free cash flow improves.

theses.expected: Muted open-to-open change near flat with a coin-flip outcome
theses.mechanism: A large implied move is already priced and the semis sector tone is supportive, so outcomes depend on small guidance differences.
theses.wrong_if: The gap exceeds about 5% in either direction at the open.

key_observations: Q4 revenue and gross margin guidance versus consensus
Foundry external customer wins and 14A commitments
DCAI growth and CPU supply constraints
Any commentary on the Classiq deal and dilution
